text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/11/17 - Essay - 01
A musician holds a guitar.
Pexels · 18390140
Listening without distraction
There is more than one way to listen to a whole album. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful
starting points.
One reason is that setting aside distractions lets us notice more of the music. For instance, we put the phone away during the first
song. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that sharing different preferences makes listening more interesting. For example, each friend chooses one track
and explains what they enjoy about it. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that
different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Discuss the claim that more preparation always helps people listen to a whole album. Support a qualified position with two concrete
examples. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the
situation; discuss setting aside distractions lets us notice more of the music with an example; discuss sharing different preferences
makes listening more interesting with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
